THE ECHO COLOSSEUMnProprietor: D. Marlow, late of Kiteholm.nFights nightly. (It is always night.)
The great lamp turns slowly, throwing its beam not out to sea but straight down into the rift.
Somewhere far below, something that has never had a shape turns its face away from the light, and sleeps on.
Steps cut into the cliff, going down into a dark so thick it looks wet. Someone has scratched beside them: 30 FLIGHTS. NO RAIL.
RANKS I–X. ONE MEMORY EACH.nPrizes for first victories only.nThe management is not responsible for anything you remember.
(It cheers, a beat after everyone else, for a fight that happened years ago.)
(It is booing someone. You check. It is booing you. It is the memory of someone who lost money on you.)
(It mouths a name, over and over. Not yours. Not anyone's anymore.)
